title: Smallest Falling Path Sum

content.inputFormat: Single line: JSON array of all arguments, e.g. [arg1, arg2, ...]

sampleTestCases.explanation: There are two falling paths with a minimum sum as shown.
The falling path with a minimum sum is shown.

content.problemStatement:
With an `n x n` array of integers `matrix`, output *the **smallest sum** of any **falling path** through* `matrix`.

A **falling path** starts at any element in the first row and chooses the element in the next row that is either directly below or diagonally left/right. Specifically, the next element from position `(row, col)` will be `(row + 1, col - 1)`, `(row + 1, col)`, or `(row + 1, col + 1)`.

**Example 1:**

![](https://assets.leetcode.com/uploads/2021/11/03/failing1-grid.jpg)

```
Input: matrix = [[2,1,3],[6,5,4],[7,8,9]]
Output: 13
Explanation: There are two falling paths with a minimum sum as shown.
```

**Example 2:**

![](https://assets.leetcode.com/uploads/2021/11/03/failing2-grid.jpg)

```
Input: matrix = [[-19,57],[-40,-5]]
Output: -59
Explanation: The falling path with a minimum sum is shown.
```

**Constraints:**

* `n == matrix.length == matrix[i].length`
* `1 <= n <= 100`
* `-100 <= matrix[i][j] <= 100`

solution.approach: Use dynamic programming. For each cell in row i, add the minimum cumulative path sum among the three reachable cells directly above, above-left, and above-right. The matrix is updated in place, so the last row contains the minimum cumulative sum for every possible ending column.

better.complexity: O(n^2) time and O(n^2) auxiliary space.
better.description: Store the minimum falling-path sum reaching every cell in a separate n x n DP table. For cell (i,j), use matrix[i][j] plus the minimum of the reachable cells from row i-1.

optimal.complexity: O(n^2) time and O(1) auxiliary space, excluding the input matrix.
optimal.description: Apply the same DP recurrence directly to the input matrix, overwriting each cell with its minimum cumulative falling-path sum. For each position, consider only the valid three predecessors. The answer is the minimum value in the final row.

bruteForce.complexity: O(3^n) time and O(n) recursion space.
bruteForce.description: Enumerate every possible falling path from the first row to the last row and return the minimum sum. Each row can branch to up to three columns, so the number of paths grows exponentially with n.

followUps: Can the dynamic-programming table be reduced from O(n^2) extra space to O(n) extra space?
Can the solution be implemented without allocating any additional DP array?
What changes if the allowed next-row moves include a larger horizontal range?
Can you implement the recurrence using two one-dimensional arrays instead of modifying the input?
